description: We are Alcyone Team, a group of space enthusiasts who are passionate about science, technology, and creative problem solving. Our team is working fully online, so you can join us from anywhere in the world.
summary: Project ALCYONE is an educational website that tells the stories of hardware NASA has left across the solar system since the 1960s. Some of it completed its mission, some is still working, and some is no longer active. Our site introduces school-age space enthusiasts to this equipment and the science it made possible. Content is organized into three worlds: the Moon (Apollo science equipment), Mars (rovers and instruments), and deep space (probes still travelling away from Earth). Each section uses storytelling, real archive images, and audio with voiceover, so young learners can follow each machine's journey in a clear and engaging way. We built the site with HTML and CSS, using NASA images and information from NASA's archive.
details:
What it does: A multi-page website, with an introduction page and one page for each of the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Each page presents selected pieces of hardware through narrative text, images, and voiceover audio.

Benefits and intended impact: It makes space history and science accessible to school-age children, and shows that every machine has a different story and status.

Tools: HTML and CSS for the website.

Creativity: We turn technical mission information into stories for children instead of a plain list of facts.

Team work: Research, writing, and voiceover; interface design; and web development, each handled by different team members.
